# Neighborhood Repair Pilot
## Need
The Riverside public library receives repeated requests for basic bicycle repairs, but its current events offer no repair service.
## Offer
The library will host a weekly repair table in the ground-floor workshop during a ten-week pilot.
## Capacity
Two volunteer mechanics will attend each Saturday session and may accept at most twelve bicycles per day.
## Measures
The coordinator will record completed repairs, items declined, and whether a visitor returns within thirty days.
## Decision
The library board reviews the ten-week results on 18 June 2027 and decides whether to continue the service.

# River Access Maintenance Review
## Overview
This review records inspection routines, completed work, gaps, and a July follow-up for the east-bank path.
## Purpose
This internal review records how the maintenance schedule changed after responsibility for the east-bank footpath moved from the parks unit to the riverside operations team. The note is intended to help the new team understand the current schedule before it proposes any changes.
## Why the handoff changed the inspection rhythm for the east-bank path
Before the handoff, parks staff walked the route every second Tuesday and filed a short checklist at the end of the shift. Operations staff inherited the route in February and added a visual check after heavy rain. The two routines overlap, but they inspect different failure points: the first catches loose rail fasteners and the second checks runoff channels and standing water.
## Work completed since February
The team replaced six rail fasteners, cleared three drainage grates, and repainted two distance markers. A second inspection found one grate blocked again after leaf fall. The work log records completed work separately from observations that still need a crew visit.
## Open questions for the next review
The route has no fixed rainfall threshold for an extra inspection. The parks unit used local judgment, while the operations checklist asks staff to record rain only as light, moderate, or heavy. A shared threshold would make the two logs easier to compare, but this source does not set one.
## Evidence limits
The February-to-May log covers twelve scheduled walks and four weather-triggered checks. It does not contain visitor counts, injury reports, or a cost comparison with the prior year. Any conclusion about safety or budget impact would need another source.
## Next review date
The operations lead will review the combined checklist with parks staff on 14 July 2027. The meeting agenda includes route ownership, rainfall wording, and whether the repeat grate blockage needs a separate work order.

# Mobile Library Route Options
## Overview
The county is comparing three routes for a six-month mobile library trial.
## Decision context
The source team has not selected a route and has not estimated demand outside the listed stops.
## North Loop
The North Loop covers 18 kilometres and visits four stops. It needs 3.5 driver hours per service day. Its two rural stops have no indoor waiting area.
## Market Link
The Market Link covers 12 kilometres and visits five stops. It needs 4.0 driver hours because the central market stop has a scheduled 45-minute dwell. A school asked for a later arrival, but no change has been approved.
## Lakeside Spur
The Lakeside Spur covers 21 kilometres and visits three stops. It needs 3.0 driver hours. One bridge has a posted 7.5-tonne limit, and the source does not state the vehicle's loaded weight.
## Recorded comparison
North Loop has the longest list of stops among the two rural options, Market Link has the most stops overall, and Lakeside Spur has the longest distance. These measures describe the route sheet only; they do not establish which route serves more readers.
## Trial review
The trial coordinator will bring mileage, visit counts, and missed-stop reports to the 9 October 2027 review. No route cost or attendance forecast appears in this note.

# Archive Intake Process Note
## Overview
This fictional process note covers archive intake and exception handling.
## Purpose
This process note describes a fictional archive intake workflow. The long paragraphs are included to stress text fitting in a narrow content region.
## Receipt and first check
When a package arrives, the intake clerk records the delivery date, the sending office, and the number of containers before opening any container. The clerk checks whether the package includes a transfer list and places a temporary identifier on each box. If a list is missing, the clerk records that fact and keeps the package in the review queue until the sending office responds.
## Description and restriction review
An archivist compares the container labels with the transfer list, then records a brief description of each series. The review also checks whether a donor agreement, privacy restriction, or handling condition accompanies the material. A restriction is recorded with its exact wording and review date; the clerk does not infer an end date when the agreement is silent.
## Location assignment
After the description is checked, the records manager assigns a shelf location and updates the location register. Oversize items receive a separate location entry because they are stored in a different room. The register records the identifier, shelf, date, and staff initials so another worker can trace a later move.
## Exception handling
Damaged containers, missing lists, and uncertain ownership go to the exception queue. Staff attach a note describing what they observed and who needs to answer the question. The workflow does not permit staff to discard material while an ownership question remains open.
## Completion record
The intake is complete when the description, restriction review, and location entries are all present. The source note defines no target processing time and gives no annual intake volume, so those measures cannot be inferred from this workflow.

## Process overview
This fictional procedure describes how a community workshop lends shared equipment. It is a process description, not a service performance report.
## Request
The member submits an item request with a preferred pickup date. The coordinator checks that the member record is active before reserving equipment.
## Availability
The storekeeper checks the reservation board and inspects the item. If it is already reserved or needs repair, the storekeeper records the reason and offers an available date only when one is listed.

At pickup, the member and storekeeper compare the item identifier with the checkout form. Both initial the condition field before the item leaves the workshop.
## Return
The storekeeper checks the returned item against the checkout form and records any missing parts or damage. The member receives a copy of the return note.
## Closeout
The coordinator closes the reservation after the return record is filed. The source defines no loan duration or late-return fee.

The demo sheet B-03 lists 8 cancelled bookings in January, 11 in February, 9 in March, 13 in April, 12 in May, and 10 in June.
## Units and relationship
Bookings and cancellations are event counts. Attendee visits count people entering a room, so one booking may include several visits. The series should not share a single unlabelled unit.

Each sheet is generated fixture data with a B-01, B-02, or B-03 label. It contains no workbook export from an external organization.
